title: Refresh and Content Opportunity Scoring Using Historical Search Signals: A Leakage-Safe Grouped-Client Machine Learning Study
author: Zafar Ullah and Afaq Ahmad Khan
affiliation: Department of Computer Science, University of Engineering & Technology Mardan, Pakistan
abstract: Editorial teams responsible for large websites rarely have enough time to examine every page that loses or underuses search visibility. This study therefore asks which eligible pages should appear first in a human review queue when only historical prediction-time search signals are available. The analysis used 9,841,378 anonymized daily observations from March 2026 and 331,437 client-page pairs; fixed eligibility rules retained 34,038 pages from 32 clients. Signals from March 1-15 were separated from a later-impression proxy defined over March 16-31. A frozen position-adjusted CTR and visibility baseline, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest were evaluated on the same grouped-client holdout. Logistic Regression measured Precision@50 of 0.640, compared with 0.520 for the baseline and 0.540 for Random Forest, with zero client overlap. A deliberately invalid outcome-derived feature raised Average Precision from 0.3939 to 0.9999, showing how future information can invalidate an evaluation. The output is a reason-coded queue for human review, not an automatic refresh system or a causal estimate of editing impact.
